def: Looking at data with open questions, through summaries, plots and audits, before committing to a model.
The delay before a case's true outcome is known, which makes recent rows look better than they are because their outcomes are incomplete.
Missing completely at random: whether a value is missing is unrelated to any observed or unobserved data.
Missing at random: whether a value is missing depends only on other observed columns.
Missing not at random: whether a value is missing depends on the missing value itself.
A special number such as 999 or -1 stored in place of a missing or unknown value.
A row or item that differs from another only trivially, so that having both in training and test sets inflates validation scores.
A difference between the distribution a model was trained on and the one it is applied to.
A change in the distribution of the inputs while the relationship between inputs and target stays the same.
A change over time in the relationship between the inputs and the target.
The largest gap between the empirical cumulative distributions of two samples, used to score how much a feature has shifted.
A drift score that bins a feature by training quantiles and sums the log-ratio-weighted differences in bin shares between two datasets.
Training a classifier to tell training rows from test rows; an accuracy well above chance reveals how and where the sets differ.
Using information in a feature that would not be available at prediction time, producing unrealistically good validation scores.
